\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{वज़न} (vazan)}{वज़न (vazan)}]{\hi{वज़न} (vazan) — weight}

\label{lesson:HI-C411-vazan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for customs, then the Hindi for a fee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{वज़न}}
\textbf{\hi{वज़न}} — \emph{vazan} — \textquotedblleft{}weight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{मेरे} \hi{सामान} \hi{का} \hi{वज़न} \hi{बीस} \hi{किलो} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mere sāmān kā vazan bīs kilo hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My luggage weighs twenty kilos.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{वज़न}} (\emph{vazan}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{wazn}, \textquotedblleft{}weight, weighing\textquotedblright{}, through Persian; Hindi breaks up the final zn with a vowel.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vazan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vazan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mere sāmān kā vazan bīs kilo hai.} — My luggage weighs twenty kilos.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for customs, then the Hindi for a fee, then say \emph{vazan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{वज़न} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Weight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{विलंब} (vilamb)}{विलंब (vilamb)}]{\hi{विलंब} (vilamb) — a delay (formal)}

\label{lesson:HI-C411-vilamb}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a fee, then the Hindi for weight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{विलंब}}
\textbf{\hi{विलंब}} — \emph{vilamb} — \textquotedblleft{}a delay (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{ट्रेन} \hi{दो} \hi{घंटे} \hi{के} \hi{विलंब} \hi{से} \hi{आई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭren do ghaṇṭe ke vilamb se āī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train came two hours late.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{विलंब}} (\emph{vilamb}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{vilamba}, \textquotedblleft{}hanging down\textquotedblright{} and so \textquotedblleft{}slowness, delay\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams); announcements use it where talk says \hi{देर}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vilamb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vilamb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭren do ghaṇṭe ke vilamb se āī.} — The train came two hours late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a fee, then the Hindi for weight, then say \emph{vilamb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{विलंब} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A delay (formal)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{पेटी} (peṭī)}{पेटी (peṭī)}]{\hi{पेटी} (peṭī) — a belt (a seat belt)}

\label{lesson:HI-C411-peti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for weight, then the Hindi for a delay (formal).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पेटी}}
\textbf{\hi{पेटी}} — \emph{peṭī} — \textquotedblleft{}a belt (a seat belt)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{विमान} \hi{उतरने} \hi{तक} \hi{अपनी} \hi{पेटी} \hi{मत} \hi{खोलिए।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimān utarne tak apnī peṭī mat kholiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Do not undo your seat belt until the plane has landed.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\hi{पेटी} is also a small box or chest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{पेटी}} (\emph{peṭī}) goes back to \emph{*pēṭṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}belly\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 8376), which lists Hindi \emph{peṭ}, the belly, and \emph{peṭī}, \textquotedblleft{}a girth\textquotedblright{}, the band round a horse's belly; the seat belt is the newest band of all. The box called \hi{पेटी} may be a different word: CDIAL notes look-alike words for a basket.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peṭī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peṭī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimān utarne tak apnī peṭī mat kholiye.} — Do not undo your seat belt until the plane has landed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for weight, then the Hindi for a delay (formal), then say \emph{peṭī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पेटी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A belt (a seat belt)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{रद्द} (radd)}{रद्द (radd)}]{\hi{रद्द} (radd) — cancelled}

\label{lesson:HI-C411-radd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a delay (formal), then the Hindi for a belt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{रद्द}}
\textbf{\hi{रद्द}} — \emph{radd} — \textquotedblleft{}cancelled\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{आँधी} \hi{की} \hi{वजह} \hi{से} \hi{उड़ान} \hi{रद्द} \hi{हो} \hi{गई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā̃dhī kī vajah se uṛān radd ho gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight was cancelled because of the storm.
\end{quote}

\hi{रद्द} \hi{होना}, to be cancelled; \hi{रद्द} \hi{करना}, to cancel.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{रद्द}} (\emph{radd}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{radd}, \textquotedblleft{}a turning back, a rejection\textquotedblright{}, through Persian. It does not change: \hi{उड़ान} \hi{रद्द} \hi{हुई}, \hi{ट्रेन} \hi{रद्द} \hi{हुई}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{radd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{radd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā̃dhī kī vajah se uṛān radd ho gaī.} — The flight was cancelled because of the storm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a delay (formal), then the Hindi for a belt, then say \emph{radd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{रद्द} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Cancelled\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{प्रस्थान} (prasthān)}{प्रस्थान (prasthān)}]{\hi{प्रस्थान} (prasthān) — departure (formal)}

\label{lesson:HI-C411-prasthan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a belt, then the Hindi for cancelled.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{प्रस्थान}}
\textbf{\hi{प्रस्थान}} — \emph{prasthān} — \textquotedblleft{}departure (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{प्रस्थान} \hi{से} \hi{पहले} \hi{अपना} \hi{सामान} \hi{जाँचिए।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{prasthān se pahle apnā sāmān jā̃ciye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Check your luggage before departure.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{प्रस्थान}} (\emph{prasthān}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{prasthāna}, \textquotedblleft{}setting out, departure\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): the partner of \hi{आगमन} on every departures board.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prasthān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prasthān se pahle apnā sāmān jā̃ciye.} — Check your luggage before departure.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a belt, then the Hindi for cancelled, then say \emph{prasthān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
